I found nothing in this file that the proof-simplification rubric would justify changing. I read all 37 lines. The file contains seven certificate theorems, `computeRow_22_9_21_0` through `computeRow_22_9_21_6`. Each one states that `RowCompute.yRowIntegralFast 22 9 21 (RowCompute.rows[i]!) = 0`, and each is proved by a single `decide +kernel`.

I also read the definitions of `yRowIntegralFast` and `rows` in `lean/OAI/Analysis/Laughlin/FourBody/RowCompute.lean`. `yRowIntegralFast` is a double sum over a list of concrete integer data, so these are closed computations. Checking them in the kernel is the shortest and clearest proof available. There are no intermediate steps, case splits or rewrites to remove, and no named lemma would make the proofs simpler.

One possible change would be to merge the seven theorems into a single statement over all indices. That would change the API rather than simplify a proof. `GramData22.lean` (line 577) uses each theorem by name, so a merge would mean rewriting that call site too, and the rubric doesn't cover that kind of change. I don't see anything left uncertain about this file.
